attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The branch still lacks certified values or rigorous enclosures for the five endpoint partition-function evaluations and for the same-theory tail T_tail in the continuum scaling window.
steps: Start from the corrected Schur-Feshbach scalar in a post-H,K null vector z; only the connected endpoint part of R can still lower the form.
Use the heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulator and decompose the reflected Wilson cumulant into Wick-square pairings, straight f f commutator contacts, endpoint boxes, and exterior tails.

Discard no dangerous negative term in the first two pieces: Wick-square terms are positive Gram contributions included in M_G, and straight f f contacts vanish under the null-incidence identity on non-corner plaquettes.
Compress all endpoint color/geometric incidence into a single singlet source direction xi_v(z), so the needed cumulant is the scalar fourth derivative d^4/ds^4 log Z_v(s xi_v(z)) at s=0.
Apply the symmetric five-point fourth-difference formula. Taylor expansion gives the exact h^2 M_6/6 remainder because the sixth-power stencil moment equals 120.
Combine endpoint intervals with the explicit prefactor (g^4/4)(T_F/N)^2 and the tail enclosure T_tail, then compare M_G+R_end with zero.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The finite-difference lemma is valid conditional on analytic source bounds and tail control, but no signed computation of log Z_v(qh xi_v(z)) has yet been performed; the crude heat-kernel M_6 bound may also be too lossy as a -> 0.

assumptions: The regulator is the heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulator at lattice spacing a, with endpoint box radius r satisfying a << r and containing every corner plaquette touched by the reflected collar collapse.
z is normalized, z perpendicular to the vacuum vector e, and z lies in ker(PHP) for the corrected post-H,K finite block.
Wick-square contractions are kept in the safe positive margin M_G(z), while straight-segment f f commutator contacts cancel by the null-incidence identity away from endpoint boxes.
The endpoint source functional log Z_v(eta) is analytic for |eta| <= 2h||xi_v(z)|| and has a certified sixth directional derivative bound M_{6,v}(z).
The omitted exterior of endpoint boxes has a same-theory tail bound |Tail_{r,a}(z)| <= T_tail(r,a,z) for the same Wilson observables.
definitions: source object: heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulated reflected Wilson hairpin endpoint boxes, with singlet flux sources coupled to the same lattice action as the collar observables.
target object: a certified lower and upper interval for the post-H,K endpoint contribution to the corrected Schur-Feshbach null-channel quadratic form.
controlled interface: central fourth source differences of log endpoint-box partition functions give the connected four-flux boundary cumulant with an explicit sixth-derivative error.

same-theory condition: the endpoint boxes, sources, Wilson trace normalization, and collar-to-boundary limit use the locked gauge-invariant Wilson algebra without boundary counterterms or altered renormalization.
Phi_{v,alpha} denotes the oriented singlet boundary flux insertion in endpoint box v, including the Wilson expansion sign convention and color trace normalization.
epsilon_{i,v,alpha} is the oriented incidence of hairpin i at endpoint v in flux channel alpha; xi_v(z)=sum_i z_i epsilon_{i,v,alpha} is the compressed null-channel source.
M_G(z) is the already extracted positive corrected Schur-Feshbach margin from Gaussian/Wick-square safe terms, not a new symbolic threshold.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Evaluate log Z_v at sources 0, +/-h xi_v(z), +/-2h xi_v(z). If the certified interval I_S lies strictly below zero, the finite Wilson block is a same-theory OS falsifier; if it lies above zero, the endpoint-box obstruction is promoted as harmless for this block.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma converts the remaining post-H,K R/kappa_4 endpoint-box term into five regulator-level source evaluations per endpoint, with an explicit error interval and a valid promotion/falsifier test.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For the locked three-hairpin post-H,K null channel, the dangerous connected boundary-OPE polarization R is certified by scalar fourth source differences of heat-kernel endpoint-box partition functions. Full kappa_4 diagonalization is unnecessary unless the Feshbach null space has dimension greater than one.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if endpoint finite differences or tail bounds cannot be defined in the locked Wilson algebra without adding a boundary counterterm.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote this block if rigorous intervals for all endpoint boxes give inf(M_G+I_R)>0 uniformly in the cutoff window.
control_decision.reason: This is a contribution-making move after H,K: it names the heat-kernel regulator, the connected four-flux Wilson cumulant, the Wick-square and f f cancellations, and a concrete sign/size condition for promotion or falsifier status.

dependency_updates.description: Used only through the corrected post-H,K margin M_G and the null vector z; no further obstruction-ladder restatement is needed.
Five heat-kernel endpoint partition-function values per endpoint now determine the needed kappa_4 scalar with h^2M_6/6 error.

dependency_updates.dependency_id: Wick-square and straight f f cancellation
dependency_updates.description: The cancellation is now required only before the endpoint-box split; endpoint corners are deliberately retained in Z_v.
Need a regulator-local estimate for omitted plaquette-sheet exterior terms without boundary counterterms.

falsifiers: A certified interval with sup(M_G+I_R)<0 is the direct finite-block falsifier for same-theory OS positivity.
The straight f f cancellation fails if endpoint orientation or color trace conventions make the null incidence identity false at a non-corner plaquette.
The sixth-derivative bound grows so fast with t_a^{-1} that every useful h makes the finite-difference interval wider than M_G.
The exterior tail cannot be bounded in the locked Wilson algebra without adding a boundary counterterm or changing Wilson renormalization.
Non-singlet endpoint states survive the reflected product, showing that the singlet-projected endpoint box is not a valid same-theory reduction.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: The useful next R computation is scalar, not spectral: the Feshbach null vector contracts the singlet endpoint kappa_4 before any eigenvalue problem is needed. This turns the connected Wilson boundary-OPE polarization into finite source evaluations of log Z_v and exposes the exact valid sign test: compare the certified interval for M_G+R_end with zero. The branch is not looping, but promotion now depends on actual endpoint-box data or a sharper analytic bound than the crude t_a^{-3} sixth-derivative estimate.
